Compared with an edit-distance matcher

Source: vignettes/comparison-with-alternatives.Rmd
comparison-with-alternatives.Rmd

R/agreement.R has carried this sentence since the rule was removed from the real pipeline:

No edit-distance tolerance. A one-edit rule was added and removed the same day: measured, it changed 64 of 30,740 candidate pairs and was worth 22 records, while admitting pairs that are genuinely different given names (JULIA/JULIE, LEE/LEA, ANN/ANNE).

That is a performance claim about an alternative implementation, and until now it was prose. This vignette is the measurement, on the 190 pairs of ROSTER_BENCHMARK whose truth is known by construction.

Why this is a vignette and not a function

tests/testthat/test-no-fuzzy.R refuses any approximate-matching call anywhere in R/: source scan, parse-tree scan, and call-graph reachability over the installed namespace, with no exempt module. An exported compare_with_edit_distance() was written first and the guard rejected it, correctly — a package whose argument is that approximate spelling similarity has no place in identity resolution should not ship fuzzy machinery reachable from its own namespace, not even to argue against it.

A vignette is code you can run and read, and it is outside the namespace. The comparison lives here; the rule stays absolute there.

The two approaches

The package’s decision is benchmark_decisions(): any conflicting axis rejects (a middle-name conflict excused when the roster’s middle token is the registry surname), a pair without both surname and given corroboration goes to review, a gender conflict goes to review rather than deletion.

The baseline is the simplest credible alternative and needs no new dependency: accept when the two full names are within one edit of each other.

b <- ROSTER_BENCHMARK
rules_accept <- benchmark_decisions(b) == "accept"

roster_full <- normalize_string(b$roster_name)
reference_full <- normalize_string(paste(b$npi_first, b$npi_last))
edits <- vapply(seq_along(roster_full), function(i)
  as.integer(utils::adist(roster_full[i], reference_full[i])[1, 1]), integer(1))
edit_accept <- !is.na(edits) & edits <= 1L
score <- function(accept, truth) {
  tp <- sum(accept & truth == "match")
  fp <- sum(accept & truth == "nonmatch")
  fn <- sum(!accept & truth == "match")
  data.frame(accepted = sum(accept),
             precision = round(tp / max(tp + fp, 1L), 3),
             recall = round(tp / max(tp + fn, 1L), 3),
             false_accepts = fp)
}
rbind(`mysterynpi rules` = score(rules_accept, b$truth),
      `edit distance <= 1` = score(edit_accept, b$truth))
#>                    accepted precision recall false_accepts
#> mysterynpi rules        126     1.000  0.955             0
#> edit distance <= 1       41     0.854  0.265             6

The baseline accepts a third as many true matches and makes false accepts the rules do not make.

Where the false accepts land 

false_accepts <- b[edit_accept & b$truth == "nonmatch",
                   c("family", "roster_name", "npi_first", "npi_last")]
false_accepts$edits <- edits[edit_accept & b$truth == "nonmatch"]
false_accepts
#>                      family    roster_name npi_first npi_last edits
#> 110           spelling-trap     Lee Watson       LEA   WATSON     1
#> 111           spelling-trap Elisabeth Gray ELIZABETH     GRAY     1
#> 118           spelling-trap     Dana Wells      DANA   WELLES     1
#> 121 cross-gender-derivative   Paula Gibson      PAUL   GIBSON     1
#> 122 cross-gender-derivative    Erica Mason      ERIC    MASON     1
#> 139            hub-nickname Christina Webb CHRISTINE     WEBB     1

They concentrate in the spelling-trap family, which is the JULIA/JULIE case the comment describes: one edit apart, and different people.

Where each approach loses the other’s matches 

differs <- rules_accept != edit_accept
data.frame(family = b$family[differs], truth = b$truth[differs],
           rules = ifelse(rules_accept[differs], "accept", "-"),
           edit = ifelse(edit_accept[differs], "accept", "-"))[1:12, ]
#>        family truth  rules edit
#> 1  formatting match accept    -
#> 2  formatting match accept    -
#> 3  formatting match accept    -
#> 4  formatting match accept    -
#> 5  formatting match accept    -
#> 6  formatting match accept    -
#> 7  formatting match accept    -
#> 8  formatting match accept    -
#> 9  formatting match accept    -
#> 10 formatting match accept    -
#> 11 formatting match accept    -
#> 12   nickname match accept    -

Edit distance misses what structure explains: a maiden surname in a middle slot, a nickname, concatenated initials, a credential suffix, a formatting difference. None of those are spelling errors, and a distance threshold loose enough to catch them is loose enough to accept JULIA/JULIE.

What this does not show

The corpus is built from this package’s own defect taxonomy, so clean separation is consistency, not proof of generality — the same caveat vignette("roster-benchmark") states. It also compares against one alternative. It is not a comparison with reclin2 or fastLink, which solve the scoring problem this package deliberately stops short of; DESCRIPTION draws that boundary and this vignette does not cross it.
